quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Highway signs that warn about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangerous conditions ahead. You must follow warning signs. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic instead of into it.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready for red lights, yellow lights, and cross traffic.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, other drivers must allow for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quiet noise of large trucks.
The higher speed of large trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in places where the truck driver can see you and where the truck does not block your view of traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road has multiple curves ahead.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads, you should:

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Slow down and increase your distance from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow and ice. This is the most important way to avoid crashes. Also stay farther away from the car in front of you.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly so cars and pedestrians can move out of your way.
Honk your horn to alert cars and pedestrians.
Stop and make sure no cars or pedestrians are coming before you go.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and make sure no cars or pedestrians are coming before you go.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Wait until no cars or pedestrians are approaching. This is the law.

questions.question: Your stopping distance gets longer when stopping on:
questions.explanation: Wet or icy roads make stopping distances longer. Loose gravel or stones also increase stopping distance.

questions.question: After an accident where someone is hurt, you should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press on the wound to stop it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A red traffic light is ahead.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
A green traffic light is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you traffic only moves in one direction. You must drive in the direction shown on the sign.

questions.question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not ideal.
Entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: When roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when anything else makes conditions unsafe, drive slower than the posted speed limit. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are under the limit when conditions are bad.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop and check for traffic, then go if it is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and go with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the yellow light appears, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs mean:
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle sign tells you to yield. Wait until the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians before continuing.

questions.question: Which does NOT affect the distance needed to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: Stopping distance never depends on:

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather and visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. Time of day itself does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately to let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road and stop as safely as possible.
Move slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop as safely as possible.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or sirens approaches, move as far right as safely possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you pass, check that the passing lane is clear. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: If a bus signals to re-enter the main road after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to return to the main road after picking up or dropping off passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus back into traffic safely.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. The sign will also have text to confirm this.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially if there are no lights or gates. Wait until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks before crossing. Do not change gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm and steer toward the direction the back of your vehicle is sliding.

questions.question: You may not park within ____ of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park only where it is legal and where other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or help has not arrived. Focus on your driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never drive to an accident, fire, or disaster just to look.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, a pedestrian should walk on:

options.text: The side with the lightest traffic.
The same side where traffic is moving.
The side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing traffic to see oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. This lets you stop faster and still steer your vehicle.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand upward, they are signaling that they plan to turn right. If you are following this driver, adjust your driving accordingly.

questions.question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing the street.
They may run out in front of you without looking.
They will not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: What should you do when another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If no right lane is open, wait for clear road ahead and slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass.

questions.explanation: If being tailgated and a right lane is available, move to the right. If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce speed to let the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: At any intersection, whether controlled by signs or signals or uncontrolled, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right when both arrive at the same time.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.explanation: Always plan your trip before you drive to an unfamiliar area. Know your exact destination. Check the location on a map before you start driving.

questions.question: What lights must you use when driving in rain?
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Look through your back window for pedestrians and obstacles before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially near children. Get out and check behind your vehicle before backing into or out of a driveway.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Your level of physical fitness does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, check all directions, then go through.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic signal, be ready to yield to vehicles coming from the right. Stay alert by taking your foot off the accelerator, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, what should you assume?

options.text: The driver may open the car door as you pass.
The driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver may open the door as you approach. Drive with extra caution near parked vehicles.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: When you cannot see well, slow down first. This is your safest response to poor visibility and dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow. First, let any cars and pedestrians in the intersection go.
You can drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can turn in the direction of the arrow. First, let any cars and pedestrians in the intersection go.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane to turn. Always let cars and pedestrians already in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: This triangle-shaped sign is a Yield sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and cars coming from other directions go first. You only need to stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic is moving in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic is moving in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
Traffic is moving in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic is moving in the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down so they have room in front of your car to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so they have room in front of your car to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down to give the other driver enough space to pass. This lets them complete the pass faster and more safely.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph might need up to ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Heavy tractor-trailers take much longer to stop than regular cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph may need about 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: If your car skids, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn it in the direction you want the car to go.
Turn it the opposite way from the skid.
It does not matter which direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn it in the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go. Once the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines divide lanes moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you can cross to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead. Another road is joining from the right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and let others go first.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others go if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others go if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangle sign means yield. Slow down as you reach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let cars, bikes, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.
